issues.description: Method return-type mismatch for addGuestStudents(int): the problem statement's UML and task description declare addGuestStudents(int): void (no return value), while the solution implementation declares public boolean addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) (returns a boolean). This inconsistency can confuse students about the expected method signature and behavior and may cause automated tests or graders (which expect a void method) to fail or not compile against the solution's signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across artifacts. Option A (preferred for matching the UML): change the solution implementation to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) and update the method body to perform the guest-student addition without returning a value. Option B (if boolean return is desired): update the problem statement's task description and UML to indicate addGuestStudents(int): boolean (documenting the meaning of the boolean return as success/failure), and update the template and any tests to expect a boolean return. Ensure the template, solution, UML, and any tests use the exact same signature.
